mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription: Fortinetics LLC is a compliance architecture firm working with cloud service providers entering the federal market and with defense contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information. mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription: Verdict Technologies is a regulatory compliance and governance firm. We take on the compliance work for our clients and run it, across federal authorization, commercial assurance, and AI governance, and deliver it through a client portal. We prepare and maintain the record. We do not assess, audit, or certify it. Assessment is performed by an independent assessor, and that independence is structural: the party that builds a package cannot be the party that assesses it. An agency Authorization to Operate is the decision of that agency’s authorizing official to accept the risk of running a service for their mission. That decision is theirs alone, and every agency makes its own. Where third-party conformity assessment applies, it is performed by a notified body, and certification belongs to an accredited certification body. We build and maintain what those parties examine. Nothing we produce constitutes legal advice.

servicesOffered.serviceDescription: Advisory support for organizations pursuing a FedRAMP Certified designation, and for the contractors and agencies operating federal systems. We prepare and maintain the security package across Certification Classes A through D, through the Initial Implementation Phase listing state, and through the continuous monitoring that follows. A provider chooses one path per cloud service offering — 20x, covering Classes A, B, and C, or Rev5, covering Classes B, C, and D — and we work across both. Assessment belongs to the independent assessor, and the Authorization to Operate decision belongs to the agency. System security plans covering the applicable NIST SP 800-53 baseline; Control implementation statements, written to be examined rather than skimmed; Readiness review ahead of an independent assessor; Findings and plans of action and milestones, with owners and traceability; Certification packages prepared for agency review; Continuous monitoring deliverables and periodic control assessments; FISMA reporting support; SSDF attestation records for federal software supply chain requirements; GovRAMP (formerly StateRAMP) packages for state, local, tribal, and education government cloud services.

Advisory support for organizations whose buyers require proof before they will sign. We run the readiness work, carry it through the auditor or certification body, and keep the record current between cycles. The opinion belongs to the CPA firm and the certificate to the certification body. Readiness assessment against the criteria your buyers actually invoke; Control design, implementation statements, and the evidence behind each; Risk assessments and, for ISO/IEC 27001, the statement of applicability; Findings and remediation plans with owners and dates; Evidence collection across the observation period for a SOC 2 Type II; Internal audit and management review records for a certifiable management system; HIPAA risk analysis, safeguard documentation, and policy set; Support through auditor or certification body fieldwork, and the responses it generates.

Advisory support for organizations carrying obligations under the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001. We inventory the AI systems an organization builds, embeds, and deploys, classify them with the reasoning recorded, and maintain the governance record as the rules move. Where third-party conformity assessment applies, it is performed by a notified body. An inventory of the AI systems you build, embed, and deploy; Role and risk classification for each system, with the reasoning recorded; AI system impact assessments covering effects on the people subject to them; Technical documentation and risk management records for systems in scope; Data governance records covering provenance, quality, and fitness for purpose; An AI policy and the management system records behind it; Findings and remediation plans where obligations are not yet met.

A bounded engagement for a software or cloud supplier that must evidence its security posture to a buyer. THONIS assembles the supplier's existing artefacts — attestations and certificates, test and scan results, policies, threat models, and architecture and data-flow descriptions — into one governed package, each item source-linked to what supports it and carrying its scope and currency. Deliverables include an evidence register with named owners, an exception register for what is missing or does not apply, and a response package prepared for the customer's own accountable approver. The approver is always the customer's named reviewer. This engagement excludes testing and remediation, and THONIS does not decide materiality on the customer's behalf. Scope, inputs, fee and acceptance criteria are agreed before work begins. Independent assessment and certification decisions remain with the responsible organizations.

mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription:
SecureIT is a FedRAMP Recognized Independent Assessor that also advises cloud service providers. We have performed FedRAMP assessments since 2013, so our advice is grounded in what an assessment actually requires. Our assessment and advisory practices operate under separate leadership and separate personnel.

**Who actually does the work.** You get named senior advisors, not a bench of junior analysts supervised from a distance. The people who scope your engagement are the people who run it. We will tell you plainly where your program needs to improve, and we will do it without losing sight of the product you are trying to ship and the customers you are trying to serve.

**Technical Depth.** We advise on the architecture you actually run: serverless, containers and Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, self-hosted and hybrid deployments, and multi-cloud across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and others. We work the questions that actually decide certifications rather than the ones that are easy to write about: how your FedRAMP Minimum Assessment Scope should be drawn and what that decision will cost you, which third-party information resources you have to account for, how your information flows, security categorizations, and tenant isolation will hold up under scrutiny, and where cryptographic module validation is going to bite. We have helped providers identify their information resources, define scope, write service descriptions, and build control sets. In addition, we review (or build) the code behind automated Key Security Indicator validations rather than simply telling you that you need them. If your engineers would rather talk to a technical SME than to a compliance analyst, that is how we staff.

**Technology and ecosystem.** Advice alone does not get evidence out of your systems. We run SPARC360, our own compliance orchestration platform that can produce machine readable (JSON) and human readable outputs for CR26, assist with vulnerability evaluation and reporting, and analyze configurations and activity logs from AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and other providers for control compliance or KSI metrics. Around SPARC360, we maintain partnerships across the GRC tooling ecosystem, and we are deliberately platform-agnostic. Whether you already run Vanta, Drata, Paramify, or nothing at all, our GRC engineering practice builds the last mile that turns tooling output into evidence an assessor will accept. You do not have to adopt our platform to work with us, and you are not stranded if you have already adopted someone else's.

**Current and visible.** We can walk you through the reasoning behind the Consolidated Rules for 2026, what each Key Security Indicator is actually trying to establish, and how the CR26 rules change what is expected of an existing Rev5 package. We publish whitepapers regarding program changes, participate in FedRAMP community discussions, and attend FedRAMP conferences. If you want to judge how current we are before you call us, the record is public.

**How we engage.** Most relationships start with a fixed-fee engagement, either a focused sprint against a specific need or a roadmap when you want an operating model rather than a deliverable. From there, clients move to a subscription relationship sized to how much of the compliance function they want us to carry, from periodic advisory through to running the compliance operating rhythm day to day. Billing is smoothed monthly rather than hourly, so heavier months and quieter ones even out and you are not deciding whether a question is worth a change order.
